01 / CONFIGURATION GOVERNANCEImplemented · rollout pending
CONFIGURATION / CONTROL

TCMS

A governed write path for tenant configuration.

Designed and drove an AI-assisted build of a configuration control plane: validated changes, independent approvals, immutable PostgreSQL revisions, and an etcd projection. Implemented and integration-tested; production rollout remains pending.

GoPostgreSQLetcdReactHelm
Explore the engineering +

The challenge

Tenant behavior encoded in deployment values ties routine product configuration to infrastructure changes, without a consistent approval or audit model.

My contribution

Authored the architecture, invariants and implementation specification; reviewed and integrated the AI-assisted implementation, including its admin interface and Go SDK.

Engineering decisions

PostgreSQL is the source of truth; an outbox publisher materializes effective configuration into etcd. Disjoint writer permissions and publisher guards enforce one writer per prefix. Full-value revisions support rollback and rebuilding the projection.

Delivery status

Implemented with PostgreSQL/etcd integration testing documented in the project handoff. Pilot rollout and operational impact are pending; latency and recovery objectives remain targets.

04 / TENANT ISOLATIONImplemented · integration pending

Tenant-routed OTel SDK

Route traces at the source. Fail closed.

Built a Python OpenTelemetry extension that propagates tenant identity, stamps spans, and routes exports to tenant-specific OTLP destinations. AI-assisted implementation and review; downstream integration remains pending.

PythonOpenTelemetryW3C baggageOTLP
Explore the engineering +

The challenge

Tenant context can be lost across thread and task boundaries, while centrally configured routing can lag behind tenant onboarding.

My contribution

Authored the package and integration API with AI assistance, including processor/exporter behavior, tests, lifecycle fixes and documentation review.

Engineering decisions

Use context-local identity with baggage fallback; drop unroutable spans instead of sending them to a default tenant sink. Bound exporter resources and guard against duplicate registration.

Status

The handoff reports an implemented, tested package. Consumer integration and production isolation outcomes remain unverified.

05 / CROSS-CLOUD NETWORKINGDelivered · scoped benchmark

LLM egress hub

Simplify the path to inference.

Centralized LLM egress using HAProxy and private Azure-to-AWS connectivity. TCP passthrough reached 735 requests per second versus 534 in HTTP mode in the documented single benchmark.

HAProxyAzureAWSCoreDNSIPSec
Explore the engineering +

The challenge

Per-environment egress addresses create repeated allowlisting and network-management work.

My contribution

Designed and debugged the shared egress path, proxy behavior, DNS resolution and streaming timeouts.

Engineering decisions

TCP passthrough preserves the end-to-end TLS path. DNS and SNI behavior mattered; pinned upstream addresses also introduce a rotation and maintenance trade-off.

Measured result

735 vs 534 RPS is approximately 37.6% higher throughput. The handoff describes one Apache Bench run with incomplete test conditions; this is not a repeatable fleet-wide performance guarantee.

10 / WEIGHTED POD PLACEMENTImplemented · public code

Kube SmartScheduler

Make placement intent explicit.

A Kubernetes operator using admission-time mutations and placement policies to distribute pods across node classes, with weighted strategies, base counts, drift detection and rebalancing.

GoAdmission webhooksCRDscert-manager
Review code and risk guidance ↗
Explore the engineering +

My contribution

Operator and policy implementation, webhook fixes, release work and architecture risk documentation.

Engineering decisions

Mutate placement constraints before scheduling and express shared policies through a CRD. Hard node selectors constrain eligible nodes; they are not a replacement for every native scheduler behavior.

Trade-offs

Rebalancing can interact with HPA, disruption budgets and rollouts. Public documentation recommends careful opt-in deployment; production adoption is not established.

02 / HOW I THINK

Build for the incident.
And the next engineer.

Good architecture survives contact with production. Great platforms make that easier for everyone.

01

Reliability is a design input.

Start with failure modes, SLOs and recovery paths. Use incidents to improve the system, not just restore it.

02

Make the safe path easy.

Encode guardrails in controllers, reusable IaC and GitOps. Reduce the decisions every application team has to repeat.

03

Measure before you optimize.

Benchmark, examine the bottleneck, and make the trade-off explicit. Cost, latency and isolation belong in the same conversation.
